name: Surgical Precision Game
description: A steady hand, six peculiar predicaments, and an original patient with a lot on his mind. Guide little pieces through tactile cavities without touching their rims.

settings.label: Sound requested · enable in the toy

assets.credit: Original Fine Trouble board, patient Milo and six illustrated objects

compatibility: Canvas 2D, Pointer Events, ResizeObserver and requestAnimationFrame. No external assets, fonts, services, or runtime dependencies.
Mouse, trackpad, pen and captured touch. Choose a close-up for small screens. Keyboard: choose a cavity, Space to grip or release, arrows to move, Shift for finer travel, Escape to return safely.
Hidden tabs, offscreen previews and shared pause suspend the challenge timer and return a held piece without a penalty. No catch-up or unexpected failures on return.
AudioContext is created only by the local Enable sound button. Settings restore never enables audio. The visual lamp and readable case notes provide equivalent feedback.
Reduced motion suppresses celebratory rays. Essential pointer-controlled movement remains direct, without camera animation or board shake.
notes: Fine Trouble is an original illustrated toy. Milo, a contemplative collector in striped nightclothes, carries six fictional nuisances: a tangled thought, a spare butterfly, a midnight biscuit, pocket thunder, lost marbles and a dancing screw.

Hold a piece, guide it along the marked cavity route, and release inside the end ring to lift it into the recovery tray. The ring represents the entire checked footprint; the decorative handles sit above the board. This is a two-dimensional precision game with illustrated depth.

Collision uses a swept disk against every polygon edge, including the full segment between pointer samples. A rapid motion cannot skip through a wall. A slight hit-area allowance applies only to the initial grip, never to travel.

An edge contact returns only the current piece and subtracts 25 points, with a floor of zero. Removal earns 100. Three contacts end Precision mode. Timed mode begins on an explicit Start action. Random mode shuffles original objects reproducibly per appointment.

Difficulty changes cavity width; clearance and object size change the checked radius. Lower tool sensitivity shortens tool travel relative to hand movement. Rule changes reset the appointment; finish, sound and sensitivity changes preserve progress.
Five reusable presets, setup JSON and case-note export are included. A case log is a read-only record; setup files restore settings, not a partially completed game. Everything is local.
reuse: PrecisionGame in model.js accepts independent board dimensions, polygon cavities, piece origins, lift destinations, collision radii and scoring rules. It exposes begin, move, end, advance, reset and semantic event callbacks.

createPrecisionToy(canvas, settings, hooks) adds input handling, close-up inspection, drawing and lifecycle management. Supply hooks.scene, hooks.background and hooks.piece for your own board artwork and objects.

The original illustration, optional audio, Lab UI, five presets, neutral custom-board example and complete documentation are bundled in the source export. The neutral example uses a different cavity polygon and no Tampa-specific code.
